_comment: The schedules and triggers that drive the pipeline. Reference material for your IaC — this file is not read by any code.

rules.name: ecommerce-producer-schedule
rules.description: Source 1 — wakes the producer Lambda; it does one batch per firing and returns. The cadence lives here, never in a loop inside the function.

rules.name: ecommerce-pipeline-daily
rules.description: Runs the medallion state machine for yesterday's partition, after the day is closed in UTC.

input.process_date: <yesterday, injected by the target input transformer>

rules.name: ecommerce-partner-drop
rules.description: Source 2 — starts the landing ingest job when a file lands. Drop this rule and schedule the job instead if partners send many small files: Glue bills a minimum of one minute per run.

event_source_mappings._comment: Source 1 — the streaming path. ReportBatchItemFailures is what makes a partial batch failure retry only the affected messages instead of all ten.

s3_notifications._comment: Source 2 — a partner drops a file. S3 cannot start a Glue job directly, so the notification goes through EventBridge. Note the prefix: firing on the whole bucket would re-trigger on the pipeline's own writes.

glue_crawlers._comment: Catalog the lake so Athena can query it without a schema per query. Crawl silver and gold only — bronze is raw by definition and its schema is allowed to drift.
glue_crawlers.name: ecommerce-lake-crawler

alarms._comment: The pipeline emits its own counters; these are the three worth paging on.
